task: Close a source-free imported generic member requirement with its ordered argument types.
observation: A provider containing `module Provider; export fn append_one(values): values.push(1)` builds with staged ABI-v10, but its `.mossi` records `generic_constraint 1 "values" "push" "_method_result:0"` without the ordered argument expression or arity. After deleting provider source, a consumer calling `Provider.append_one(values)` receives `TYPE_MISMATCH: builtin push(item) expects 1 arguments, got 0` because the imported Constraint has an empty argument list. A zero-argument imported `value.length()` requirement succeeds and its failure diagnostic retains `Provider.mossi` provenance.
impact: Team A can instantiate and solve ordered requirement terms when present, but source-free nonzero-argument member calls cannot close from this interface record; Team B must preserve the full constraint shape in its serializer/importer before the joint gate can pass.
evidence: ./moss check consumer/src/main.moss --json: TYPE_MISMATCH builtin push(item) expects 1 arguments, got 0

resolution.summary: Team A retains typed ordered argument terms and provider provenance when supplied. The staged interface must carry method arity and arguments; no parser or diagnostic-string reconstruction is used.

reproducer: Provider: `module Provider; export fn append_one(values): values.push(1)`. Build with `MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 ./margo build --json`, remove provider source, then check consumer `module Main; import Provider; fn main(): var values = []; Provider.append_one(values); echo values[0]` with `MOSS_MODULE_PATH` pointed to provider build/debug.
suggestion: Serialize Constraint.arity and ordered Constraint.arguments as semantic operands in the versioned interface; retain origin and parent requirement IDs.
